question: Using Table 2A-2, identify the characteristic background colors for temporary traffic control, incident management, and ETC-account-only signs.
model_answer: Direct Answer: Per Table 2A-2, temporary traffic control signs use a black legend on an orange background; incident management signs use a black legend on an orange or fluorescent pink background; and ETC-Account Only signs use a black legend on a purple background (with the use of purple restricted per Chapter 2F). Fluorescent pink for incident management signs is expressly permitted by Option provisions in Part 6, and purple ETC panels are governed by a Standard in Section 2F.03. Standards (mandatory): - "Except for ETC pictographs whose predominant background color is purple, if incorporated within the green background of a guide sign, the ETC pictograph shall be on a white rectangular or square panel set on a purple underlay panel with a white border. For rectangular ETC pictographs whose predominant background color is purple, a white border shall be used at the outer edges of the purple rectangle to provide contrast between the pictograph and the sign background color." Options (permitted): - "Warning signs used for TTC incident management situations may have a black legend and border on a fluorescent pink background." - "Guide signs used in TTC incident management situations may have a black legend and border on a fluorescent pink background." - "Detour signs in TTC incident management situations may have a black legend and border on a fluorescent pink background." - "Warning and guide signs used for TTC traffic incident management situations may have a black legend and border on a fluorescent pink background (see Figure 6O-1)." Support: - "Common uses of sign colors are shown in Table 2A-2. Color schemes on specific signs are shown in the illustrations located in each applicable Chapter." Visual evidence: - [Image 4] Table 2A-2 shows "Temporary Traffic Control" with a black legend and an "X" under the orange background column; "Incident Management" with a black legend and "X"s under both the orange and fluorescent pink background columns; and "ETC-Account Only" with a black legend and an "X⁵" under the purple background column, footnoted that purple use is restricted per Chapter 2F. - [Image 2] Figure 6O-1 illustrates incident management area signs (W3-4, W4-2, W9-3, E5-2a, M4-8a, M4-9, M4-10) with black legends on fluorescent pink backgrounds. - [Image 3] Figure 2F-8 shows guide signs for ETC Account-Only entrances using purple panels containing the ETC pictograph and the word ONLY. - [Image 5] Page 443 (Figure 2F-16) shows an ETC Account-Only toll plaza canopy sign with a purple background. - [Image 7] Page 924 (Figure 6P-12) shows temporary traffic control signs (e.g., W20-1, W20-4, W3-3) with black legends on orange backgrounds. Citations: - Table 2A-2 (p.43) - Section 2A.06 Support §3 (p.43) - Section 2F.03 Standard §2 (p.381) - Section 6H.01 Option §7 (p.798) - Section 6I.01 Option §4 (p.811) - Section 6I.02 Option §2 (p.811) - Section 6O.01 Option §10 (p.854) - Figure 6O-1 (p.855) - Figure 2F-8 (p.391) - Page 443 - Page 924
gold_answer: Temporary traffic control: orange; incident management: fluorescent pink; ETC-account-only: purple.
